section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Slope vs. Area
section_1.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as the slope of a tangent line (rate of change) and the integral as the area under a curve (accumulation). Visual: Animation of a point sliding along a curve showing the changing slope, transitioning to the shading of an area growing under the curve.
section_1.example: A squirrel gathering acorns: The rate of gathering (acorns/min) vs. total acorns accumulated.

section_2.title: The Conceptual Link: Inverse Operations
section_2.content: Define the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus as the realization that differentiation and integration are inverse processes, much like addition and subtraction. Visual: A 'Balance Scale' animation where putting an integral operator on one side and a derivative on the other keeps the original function in balance.
section_2.example: A robot's position: If you know the velocity function, integrating gives you the position; if you have the position function, differentiating gives you back the velocity.

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function
section_3.content: Introduce the area function A(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t)dt. Explain that the rate at which this area grows is exactly equal to the height of the function at that point. Visual: A vertical line sweeping across a graph; as the line moves, the area 'paints' itself, and its growth rate is visualized as the height of the curve.
section_3.example: Filling a water tank: The rate of water flow (f(t)) determines how fast the depth of the water (the area) increases.

section_4.title: Formalizing the Connection
section_4.content: Present the derivative of the accumulation function: d/dx [∫[a to x] f(t)dt] = f(x). Emphasize that this proves they are perfect opposites. Visual: An algebraic transformation showing symbols 'd/dx' and '∫' canceling each other out.
section_4.example: A speedometer (derivative) vs. an odometer (integral): The speedometer measures the instantaneous change in distance recorded by the odometer.

section_5.title: Summary & Application
section_5.content: Recap that this relationship allows us to compute complex areas without infinite summations by simply finding the 'anti-derivative.' Visual: A split-screen showing a Riemann sum (many rectangles) instantly simplifying into a single subtraction problem [F(b) - F(a)].
section_5.example: A space probe calculating its path: Using the known acceleration (derivative) to calculate the total distance traveled (integral) to reach a planet.

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define grid
